verses.text: Jesus left there and went to his hometown, with his disciples coming along.

When the Sabbath came, he began teaching in the synagogue. Many who heard him were stunned: “Where’d he get all this? What’s this wisdom he’s been given? How are these powerful works happening through him?
“Isn’t he the carpenter, Mary’s son, and James, Joses, Judah, and Simon’s brother? Aren’t his sisters right here with us?” They took offense at him.
Jesus said to them, “A prophet gets honor everywhere except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own house.”
He couldn’t do any mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
He was amazed at their lack of faith. Then he went around the villages teaching.
Jesus called the twelve over and began sending them out two by two. He gave them authority over unclean spirits.
He ordered them to take nothing for the journey except a walking stick—no bread, no bag, and no money in their belts.
They could wear sandals, but weren’t to pack an extra shirt.
He told them, “Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.
“If people won’t welcome you or listen, leave and shake the dust off your feet as a witness against them. I’m telling you, Sodom and Gomorrah will have an easier time on judgment day than that town!”
So they went out and preached that people should turn back to God.
They drove out many demons, put oil on many sick people, and healed them.
King Herod heard about Jesus, whose name was now well known. He said, “John the Baptizer has come back from the dead. That’s why these powers are at work in him.”
Others were saying, “He’s Elijah.” Still others said, “He’s a prophet, like one of the prophets from long ago.”
But when Herod heard it, he said, “That’s John. I had him beheaded, and now he’s risen from the dead.”
Herod himself had ordered John arrested and chained in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife. Herod had married her.
John had kept telling Herod, “It’s against the law for you to have your brother’s wife.”
Herodias held it against John and wanted him killed, but she couldn’t make it happen.
Herod was afraid of John, knowing he was a righteous and holy man, so he kept him safe. Hearing John speak troubled him, but he still liked listening to him.
Then the right moment came. On his birthday, Herod threw a dinner for his nobles, military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
Herodias’s daughter came in and danced, pleasing Herod and his dinner guests. The king told the young woman, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I’ll give it to you.”
He swore to her, “I’ll give you whatever you ask—even up to half my kingdom.”
She went out and asked her mother, “What should I ask for?” Her mother said, “John the Baptizer’s head.”
She hurried straight back to the king and demanded, “I want you to give me John the Baptizer’s head on a platter—right now.”
The king was deeply upset. But because of his promises and his dinner guests, he didn’t want to turn her down.
Right away, the king sent a guard and ordered him to bring John’s head. The guard went to the prison and beheaded him.
He brought the head on a platter, gave it to the young woman, and she gave it to her mother.
When John’s disciples heard, they came, took his body, and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles returned to Jesus and told him everything they’d done and taught.
Jesus said to them, “Come with me to a quiet place and get some rest.” There were so many people coming and going that they didn’t even get time to eat.
So they went off in a boat by themselves to a quiet place.
But people saw them leaving, recognized Jesus, and ran there on foot from all the towns. They arrived ahead of them and gathered around him.
When Jesus came ashore and saw the huge crowd, he felt compassion for them. They were like sheep with no shepherd, so he began teaching them many things.
Late in the day, his disciples came over and said, “This place is out in the middle of nowhere, and it’s getting late.
“Send the people away so they can go to nearby farms and villages and buy themselves food. They’ve got nothing to eat.”
But Jesus answered, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “Should we go buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and feed them?”
He asked, “How many loaves do you have? Go check.” They found out and said, “Five, and two fish.”
Jesus told everyone to sit down in groups on the green grass.
They sat down in rows, groups of a hundred and groups of fifty.
Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, and broke the loaves. He gave the pieces to his disciples to hand out, and divided the fish for everyone too.
Everybody ate and had enough.
The disciples gathered up twelve baskets full of leftover bread and fish.
Five thousand men had eaten the loaves.
Right away, Jesus had his disciples get into the boat and head ahead of him to Bethsaida, while he sent the crowd home.
After saying goodbye to them, he went up the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was out in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on land.
He saw them straining at the oars because the wind was against them. During the fourth watch of the night, he came toward them, walking on the sea, and was about to pass by.
When they saw him walking on the sea, they thought he was a ghost and screamed.
They had all seen him and were terrified. But Jesus immediately spoke to them: “Take courage! It’s me. Don’t be afraid.”
He got into the boat with them, and the wind stopped. They were completely stunned, amazed among themselves.
They still hadn’t understood what the loaves meant; their hearts were hard.
After crossing over, they landed at Gennesaret and tied up the boat.
As soon as they stepped out, people recognized Jesus.
They ran through the whole region, carrying sick people on mats to wherever they heard he was.
Wherever he went—in villages, towns, or countryside—they laid sick people in the marketplaces and begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his garment. Everyone who touched it was healed. 🙌
